title: Forward Cho becomes Hull's 12th summer signing
description: Hull City sign French forward Mohamed-Ali Cho from Ligue 1 side Nice on a five-year contract.
fullText:
Hull City have signed French forward Mohamed-Ali Cho from Ligue 1 side Nice on a five-year contract.

The 22-year-old becomes the Tigers' 12th signing of the summer as they continue to strengthen following promotion to the Premier League.

The attacker made 93 appearances for Nice, scoring 12 goals and providing 13 assists during a two-and-a-half-year spell.

Cho played for England Under-16s before switching allegiance to France, who he has represented at under-21 level.

He also has experience of playing in European competitions, having featured 13 times in the Europa League for Nice and in the Champions League for Spanish side Real Sociedad.

Born in France but raised in England, Cho made his professional debut for Angers aged 16 and became the club's youngest scorer.

Hull have spent more than £75m since beating Middlesbrough in the Championship play-off final, including a club record fee for Senegal defender Nobel Mendy.

They made a dream return to the Premier League, after nine years away, with a first ever top-flight win against Manchester United in their opener.

title: Police investigating alleged assault in Carse incident
description: An incident during which Brydon Carse was handcuffed is being investigated by Derbyshire Police, who say they are looking into allegations of assault.
fullText:
An incident during which England bowler Brydon Carse was handcuffed outside a nightclub is being investigated by Derbyshire Police, who say they are looking into allegations of assault.

The 31-year-old was briefly arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly.

The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) said the incident would be investigated by the Cricket Regulator and, as a result, Carse was removed from the England squad for the second Test against Pakistan.

He has been selected in Durham's County Championship team for their match against Gloucestershire.

On Monday, Derbyshire Police said a man had been briefly detained outside Molly Malone's bar, before being released.

"A man in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly in Derby city centre on Saturday night," said the police.

"However the man was de-arrested shortly afterwards having agreed to leave the area."

On Wednesday, the police gave a further statement, which said: "We are investigating allegations of an assault in Derby city centre.

"No arrests have yet been made and the investigation is ongoing."

Carse has been approached for a response, while the ECB has not commented.

title: Out of Matt's shadow and meeting Michael Jordan - Alex Fitzpatrick's rise
description: Alex Fitzpatrick tells BBC Sport about forging his own identity, "belonging" on the PGA Tour - and his "surreal" meeting with Michael Jordan.
fullText:
If Alex Fitzpatrick wanted a glimpse into just how life changing winning on the PGA Tour would be, he did not have to wait long.

While celebrating victory at the Zurich Classic pairs event, in tandem with his older brother and world number four Matt, at a golf club just north of Palm Beach in Florida, Alex felt a congratulatory hand on his shoulder.

"I look over and it's Michael Jordan," Fitzpatrick says. "I'm like 'wow', it's insane.

"He walks past the table. He's got a bag full of cigars, t-shirt untucked, he looks like the coolest person ever.

"He walked past me, saw Gary Woodland, who won the previous week, and was like 'wow, it's a room of winners in here'. That was the coolest thing ever.

"When I started to really love basketball, I watched videos of him. I love his shoes. I loved everything about him. It was surreal having that moment.

"I'm not someone who gets starstruck but Michael Jordan, having him say stuff to me, it was a different world."

It is a world, though, where Fitzpatrick is looking very much at home.

In addition to his maiden DP World Tour win at the Indian Open in March, Fitzpatrick has five top-10 finishes in 13 starts on the PGA Tour.

While cynics were questioning the merit of receiving a two-year tour card as a result of winning April's Zurich Classic, 2026 has seen Fitzpatrick prove his place alongside the world's best.

And so sure is he of his spot among the elite, Fitzpatrick hasn't actually leaned much on 2022 US Open champion Matt for advice.

"The truth is, we haven't spoken that much about a lot of stuff. I've picked his brain once this year, maybe twice," he says.

"I feel comfortable out here and comfortable around the group of people playing on this tour.

"I've been doing this a long time, I've been playing golf since I was four.

"I haven't asked him a lot of questions about how things work, maybe how to get better with certain things.

"He's always someone I can text or call but he's still my brother and that's more important than the golf side."

When Netflix featured Alex in season two of its fly-on-the-wall documentary Full Swing, the episode was titled 'In The Shadows', and, whether on request of the production crew or not, he introduced himself as "Matt Fitzpatrick's brother" first, then "professional golfer".

This season, the younger Fitzpatrick has been carving his own path.

He followed up the Indian Open and Zurich Classic successes by finishing tied for ninth at the Cadillac Championship in May. He was then fourth at the Truist Championship at Quail Hollow and it was at that tournament in North Carolina when he felt like he belonged at this level.

"I've always had the self belief that I could compete against the best players, but I never had the chance or facts to back up my own belief," he says.

"It was nice to feel like I'm out here for a good reason. At that point, I was confident in my game and at that point I felt I could carry on."

He says his remarkable rise from outside the world's top 250 to number 68 in just 12 months was "kick-started" by working with Matt's former coach Mike Walker on a more permanent basis.

Fitzpatrick adds that "backing himself" was his best decision but does he feel like he has finally forged his own standing in the game?

"I have my own identity," he says. "This year I've really worked on what I want to achieve and who I am as a person.

"That's the big step I've taken. The success on the course doesn't define me."

With the qualification period for the 2027 Ryder Cup starting this week, both brothers could play their way into Luke Donald's European team to face the United States at Adare Manor next September.

But Fitzpatrick's immediate attention is on a strong finish at the PGA Tour's season-ending Tour Championship in the FedEx Cup play-offs.

The Sheffield golfer will tee it up on Thursday sitting 24th in the standings, with a guaranteed £260,000 even if he finishes last in the 30-man field at East Lake, capping off a year he describes "about as life changing as you can imagine".

Such has been his progress, simply playing in Atlanta, something which the likes of Justin Thomas, Shane Lowry and Rickie Fowler are not doing, is quite the achievement for the man ranked 291st in the world last August.

Whether it's playing in the biggest, most lucrative tournaments in golf, or rubbing shoulders with basketball royalty, the feelings for Fitzpatrick are the same.

"It's very surreal," he says. "I'm just trying to take it all in and make the most of it."

title: Cherki faces fight for Man City starting spot
description: Rayan Cherki saved Enzo Maresca from a losing start as Manchester City manager - but will he get the game time he wants?
fullText:
Rayan Cherki appeared off the bench against Bournemouth on Sunday and helped turn the game around for Manchester City in a dramatic comeback win.

Manager Enzo Maresca will have been relieved by the France playmaker's assists that ensured he won his first Premier League game in charge of City rather than lost it.

But Cherki himself was clearly not happy at starting the game on the bench. He came on to the pitch with a point to prove, swinging in the corner for Marc Guehi's equaliser and brilliantly setting up Josko Gvardiol's added-time winner.

City travel to Crystal Palace on Friday and the 23-year-old will hope his cameo against the Cherries was enough to earn him a start.

"He made an impact the other day," Maresca told BBC Sport in his pre-match media conference. "In terms of quality, he is a different player to the rest because he can give us moments when we struggle in the last third.

"He has the quality that we need, but it depends also on the game plan and the opponent that we play.

"There is no doubt he's going to help now and in the future. I am very happy with the way he is working."

Cherki seemed in good spirits on Tuesday evening when posing for pictures and signing autographs for fans at the PFA awards in Manchester, where he was named in the Team of the Year and nominated for the Young Player of the Year award.

His goal contributions last weekend mean he has now provided 12 assists from open play since the start of last season - more than any other Premier League player during that period.

But despite his creativity, Cherki is yet to become a regular starter for City.

Under former manager Pep Guardiola last season he made 33 Premier League appearances - but 14 of those were as a substitute.

At this summer's World Cup, he played a bit-part role - albeit he is competing against a star-studded array of France forwards.

His only start was against England in the third-fourth place play-off and he was replaced at half-time with his side 4-0 down.

That took his game time to 124 minutes across the whole tournament and videos emerged of Cherki showing apparent displeasure at coach Didier Deschamps.

Maresca admitted after Sunday's victory that Cherki is not a man to hide his feelings.

"Rayan is quite a nice and clear boy, if he is not happy he wants to show it. If he's next to me and he's not happy, you all realise that he is not happy because he is doing anything just to show that he is not happy."

In City's recent documentary on Amazon, chief executive Ferran Soriano revealed there were question marks over Cherki's attitude before he was signed from Lyon for £30m in June 2025.

"The information on Cherki was not so positive, I will be very honest," said Soriano. "Everybody knew about his abilities, but there was this idea that he was chaotic."

Maresca was seen striding towards Cherki at full-time on Sunday, before placing his arms around the player's shoulders and appearing to relay some sort of lecture.

What was said between the pair has not been made public and when asked afterwards if the forward would start a game soon, the Italian replied by saying "absolutely, yeah".

Cherki's biggest challenge this season might be to keep his emotions in check and his spirits high if the flamboyant but fiery playmaker has to wait longer than he feels he should for a regular place in City's starting line-up.

title: Are Moyes and Everton's owners on same page?
description: David Moyes said he was surprised Everton's owners regarded missing out on Europe last season as "failure". Phil McNulty asks if they are they on the same page.
fullText:
Everton's owners the Friedkin Group are rarely seen and barely heard – so when they announced via chief executive Angus Kinnear that they regarded missing out on European football last season as "failure" it came as a surprise.

Not least to manager David Moyes.

Everton were in one of the nine European places on offer to English clubs when Merlin Rohl gave them the lead against Sunderland in their penultimate game of last season.

Instead, in keeping with a collapse that saw them fail to win any of their last seven league games, Everton lost 3-1 at home to the Europe-bound Black Cats, before a final-day defeat at Tottenham Hotspur left them in 13th place.

In an interview with BBC Radio Merseyside, Kinnear said: "They viewed it as a failure because it was a failure.

"The Friedkins are winners. They want to win and we didn't win anything."

Moyes' response when this was put to him was intriguing – and begs the question whether the 63-year-old Scot is on the same page as Everton's American powerbrokers - who also own Italian club Roma - when it comes to ambition.

He said: "I'm surprised they were disappointed because there was never, ever any time anyone said to me 'David, you have to make Europe or you have to be in and around the top end'.

"I think everybody wanted to make sure we moved into the new stadium safe and with not having too difficult a season and we certainly did that last year."

Kinnear also said: "We have definitely had discussions with the ownership and David about how we use the Carabao Cup and FA Cup to give the fans something to really cheer and get behind."

Former Everton and England midfield man Leon Osman told BBC Sport: "I was a bit surprised at the statement and at the timing because, as Moyes said, I don't think anyone was saying for much of last season that not getting into Europe was a failure.

"I do think when you get on the cusp of something and it slips away, it can feel like you've failed, but I would call it a disappointment rather than a failure because so often in the last five years, before David Moyes took over, Everton have been trying to keep their heads above water by staying in the Premier League."

He added: "Of course everyone associated with Everton was disappointed because excitement was building but take a step back and look at clubs who did get into Europe, like Brighton and Bournemouth. They have been building steadily over years to put themselves in the position to make that last stride.

"I think Everton have done good business this summer and maybe if they can do more before the close of the window they might be in a better position to make that step."

Moyes bristled, questioning whether journalists were "dead stupid" when asked about the importance of cup competitions, and spirits will have been lifted by the convincing second-round Carabao Cup win at Preston North End.

Kinnear said in the same interview that Everton's squad was "in a good place" – although added there was work to do.

Moyes sounded a markedly more cautious note, warning fans not to get carried away with an opening Premier League win against Crystal Palace and victory at Deepdale.

It is clear Moyes wants TFG to deliver more backing before the transfer window closes to improve, and bolster, a squad which ran out of steam so badly last season.

He said: "For us to be a side which is competitive, I still think we have got a lot of work to do. Hopefully we are able to try and do some of it.

"We need more players. Our squad is not big enough and we need to get more quality in some areas if we can do.

"I'm not sure we will, but it's not for me and the want of trying, that's for sure."

The messages were certainly mixed, adding to a summer of mixed fortunes in the transfer market, that even led to Prime Minister and fanatical Evertonian Andy Burnham to comment on one of the hot topics when he said: "There is one thing I would just ask, sign a right-back."

This is what makes the final few days of the transfer window so vital for Moyes, who is in the final year of his contract, and Everton.

And it will not simply be about incomings. Moyes will be desperate to hang on to Iliman Ndiaye, the inspirational forward who has been central to his plans.

Everton have signed the PFA Championship player of the year Hayden Hackney from Middlesbrough. Christian Norgaard will provide experience from Arsenal as a replacement for departed veteran Idrissa Gueye, while deals for young German Merlin Rohl and England under-21 winger Tyrique George, on loan last season, were confirmed. Brennan Johnson arrived from Crystal Palace in a straight swap with Dwight McNeil.

Moyes, however, makes it plain he does not think this is enough.

So now Everton's fans must wait to see if owners, chief executive and manager can reach a meeting of minds to give Moyes what he wants and demonstrate exactly what TFG's ambitions are.

Dan Friedkin, the club's billionaire chairman, has not attended any Everton games and while absences are not uncommon among American owners, there still lurks a suspicion among Toffees' fans that TFG's interest is more piqued by their Serie A giants Roma, who are in the Champions League.

And despite such a promising start, questions still remain, especially that vexed matter of a right-back that has become such a bone of contention among Everton fans.

Moyes is believed to favour Strasbourg's Guela Doue, but this appears to have fallen down on financial grounds.

A move for Celtic's Canada right-back Alistair Johnston stalled when he got injured. Crystal Palace's Daniel Munoz was considered but as yet not pursued. Fulham would not entertain interest in Timothy Castagne. Aaron Wan-Bissaka was another considered but he joined Aston Villa on loan from West Ham United.

Eventually - surely - all parties will have to agree on a target and finally address this obvious flaw.

The £7m move for 32-year-old Norgaard looks smart work at a decent price, although Everton were hopeful of signing fellow Danish midfielder Morten Hjulmand from Sporting in Lisbon until Atletico Madrid stepped in.

Hackney is a classic Moyes signing, an outstanding Championship performer in the mould of those who arrived at Everton during his first spell such as Tim Cahill, Phil Jagielka and Joleon Lescott, as well as at West Ham United, when he signed Jarrod Bowen from Hull City.

Moyes clearly believes he needs more, especially as he will be well aware that he took the brunt of heavy fan criticism when Europe slipped away last season, and will look to TFG to bring him what he feels he needs.

TFG has delivered financial stability after the mayhem of the Farhad Moshiri years and has spent about £170m on players, so for this it deserves credit.

Osman added: "There will be constant noise until the right-back is signed and plenty would probably like a new number nine as well, but looking at the rest of the squad I think the club and David have done brilliant business.

"It takes five or six transfer windows minimum to get there depending on your starting point, so there is a few to go yet on that basis, so of course these last days of the window are important and you can absolutely see why David would like more players and quality in."

Moyes has made his views clear. Now can his wish align with Everton's owners to deliver?

title: Liverpool close in on £120m deal for PSG's Barcola
description: Liverpool are close to agreeing a deal with Paris St-Germain for Bradley Barcola - adding to the doubts surrounding Cody Gakpo's Anfield future.
fullText:
Liverpool are closing in on the signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris St-Germain for a fee that could rise to £120m.

Sources have indicated to BBC Sport that talks have progressed in the past 48 hours and a full agreement is now close for the France forward.

PSG had valued the 23-year-old at £145m, but Liverpool are poised to agree a package that will be worth a minimum of just over £100m and could rise to £120m based on significant individual and team success.

Barcola is right footed but prefers to play on the left wing and his likely arrival creates further doubt around Cody Gakpo's future at Anfield.

Multiple sources have told BBC Sport both Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City have shown interest in the Netherlands forward.

Liverpool are also in the market for a right winger, having explored moves for Brighton's Yankuba Minteh and Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr.

The Reds have had offers of £50m and £60m for Gambia winger Minteh rejected by Brighton.

Speaking before Saturday's game against Nottingham Forest, Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said he "cannot talk about players that, right now, are not ours".

He added: "But it is evident that we are trying to improve or try to fill that position because we don't have the numbers.

"I hope we can have good news soon but we are still not there."

Why Liverpool are ready to make Barcola third £100m signing

What strengths might Barcola bring to Anfield?

Iraola said he "cannot guarantee anything" when asked about Gakpo's future, but made it clear he wanted to keep the 27-year-old in his squad.

"[Gakpo] has been very good since he came back from the World Cup and his holiday, with a very good attitude. I hope we can keep him at that level because I think he has been very influential in our games," he said.

Barcola has become a main target for Liverpool as they look to add potency to their attack following the departures of Luis Diaz and Mohamed Salah in the past two summers.

He moved to PSG from Lyon in 2023 for a reported £38.5m and has won three Ligue 1 titles, two Champions Leagues, the French Cup twice, as well as the Uefa Super Cup and the Fifa Intercontinental Cup.

Barcola, who scored three goals for France in this summer's World Cup, can also play on the right or through the middle and could provide cover for Alexander Isak as Hugo Ekitike recovers from a serious Achilles injury.

As expected, Andoni Iraola showed respect to Paris St-Germain when the Spaniard was asked about Bradley Barcola, given the winger is not a Liverpool player yet.

However there was certainly an element of positivity when Iraola said he hoped to have "good news soon".

Barcola has been a priority for Liverpool since Yan Diomande opted for Real Madrid and the Anfield hierarchy are increasingly confident there will be no complications in the deal for what would be a record fee for a player leaving Ligue 1.

Barcola would bring star factor and inject real quality into a Liverpool attack that could become feared if last summer's expensive signings Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz can step up.

PSG view the deal as progressing "extremely well" and the Paris club can feasibly look at it as an excellent outcome, given they signed Barcola for £38m and will triple their money - if add-ons are met - for a player who is entering the last two years of his contract and has shown no willingness to sign an extension.

Barcola was often behind Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for the wide forward positions last season and PSG have added to their options in those areas this summer by signing Maghnes Akliouche and Mika Godts.

However Liverpool will be pleased with the deal too, having held firm earlier in the summer in terms of meeting PSG's valuation of £145m but eventually bringing in one of Europe's most exciting forwards.

title: Tottenham sign Man City's Marmoush on loan
description: Tottenham sign Manchester City forward Omar Marmoush on loan until the end of the season, with an obligation to make the deal permanent for £60m next summer.
fullText:
Tottenham have signed Manchester City forward Omar Marmoush on loan until the end of the season, with an obligation to make the deal permanent for £60m next summer.

The 27-year-old Egypt international will join former City team-mate Savio at Spurs, after the Brazilian moved to north London for an initial fee of £75m on Tuesday.

"Tottenham Hotspur is one of the biggest clubs in England, if not the world, and the project was very attractive to me," said Marmoush.

"I've spoken with the head coach [Roberto de Zerbi], I loved what he had to say and I'm sure our passion for the game will go very well together."

Marmoush signed for City from Eintracht Frankfurt for £59m in January 2025 and has scored 16 goals in 62 games for the club in all competitions.

After a bright start to his City career, Marmoush made 13 of his 21 league appearances last term from the bench with Norway international Erling Haaland the club's preferred central striker.

Marmoush was utilised as a second-half substitute in City's 3-0 Community Shield defeat by Arsenal and was an unused substitute in their 2-1 Premier League win over Bournemouth last Sunday.

Spurs have spent more than £312m in the transfer window this summer.

They have signed Mateus Fernandes from West Ham, Sandro Tonali from Newcastle and Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton, while defenders Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson, plus goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, have arrived on free transfers.

Speaking about their most recent arrival, De Zerbi said: "Omar is exactly the kind of player we want at this club - ambitious, hungry and determined to make a difference.

"He has incredible attacking quality but what I also love is his desire to improve and to win.

"He brings pace, intelligence and a real threat in front of goal, and I believe he can take our attacking play to another level."

title: Leyton Orient criticise badge on new Wrexham kit
description: Leyton Orient criticise Wrexham and their celebrity owners, Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac, for putting a badge on their new kit that mirrors their own.
fullText:
Leyton Orient have criticised Wrexham and their celebrity owners, Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac, for creating a badge on their new kit which mirrors their own.

Wrexham unveiled their cream coloured third strip on Wednesday, and received the Hollywood seal of approval with pictures of Reynolds and Mac modelling it on the club website.

But it was a new-look badge which raised eyebrows as Wrexham deviated from their traditional crest of two red dragons facing inward, a golden football, the Prince of Wales feathers with a coronet and motto, and Welsh flag colours.

Instead, the badge was replaced with two wyverns or dragons facing each other over a football, and looking remarkably like the crest of Orient.

Latest Wrexham news, analysis and fan views

The wyvern is the mythological defender of the Thames and sea, through the old Orient Shipping Company, and has adorned the badge of of the League One club since 1976.

Orient criticised Wrexham's badge on their social media by asking: "What you playing at @VancityReynolds @RMcElhenney?" alongside a video of former England manager Roy Hodgson using colourful language.

The criticism comes just weeks after Wrexham withdrew an anthem jacket from its club shop following backlash from its own fans over the use of a white dragon - rather than red - emblem.

title: Chelsea agree £40m deal for Atalanta defender Ahanor
description: Chelsea agree a deal worth up to £40m to sign Atalanta defender Honest Ahanor.
fullText:
Chelsea have agreed a deal worth up to £40m to sign Atalanta defender Honest Ahanor.

The 18-year-old Italian has permission to complete a medical in London and has agreed personal terms.

Chelsea first expressed an interest in the defender when they signed right-back Marco Palestra from the Serie A side in July.

It remains unclear whether Chelsea plan to involve the teenager in new manager Xabi Alonso's squad and his representatives say he could immediately move on loan to another Premier League club.

Ahanor, who mainly plays at left-back, joined Atalanta from Genoa on a three-year deal last summer for a reported fee of 16m euros, plus 4m euros in add-ons.

He made 28 appearances in Serie A for Atalanta last season, establishing himself as a regular starter. He also made his Champions League debut in a 2-1 win against Club Brugge in September.

In May, he was called up by Italy for friendly matches against Luxembourg and Greece.

Chelsea boss Alonso has been building his squad since taking over at Stamford Bridge in July, signing England midfielder Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa for a club record £117m, and adding experienced Premier League players Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson.

Chelsea face Brighton at home in the Premier league on Sunday after beating Fulham 3-2 in their opening match of the season on Monday.

title: I'll send Itauma back to high school - Hrgovic
description: Filip Hrgovic tells British heavyweight Moses Itauma he will "send him back to high school" when they fight for the vacant IBF heavyweight world title on Saturday.
fullText:
Filip Hrgovic told British heavyweight Moses Itauma he will "send him back to high school" when they fight for the vacant IBF heavyweight world title at London's O2 Arena on Saturday.

Unbeaten Itauma, 21, is aiming to become the second-youngest heavyweight world champion in history - Mike Tyson remains the youngest.

Hrgovic, 34, has repeatedly called Itauma a "kid" in the build-up, prompting the Chatham heavyweight to admit the taunts were starting to wind him up.

But Itauma played down their impact at Thursday's news conference. "At the end of the day, talk is cheap. It's schoolboy banter," he said.

An Olympic bronze medallist with an extensive amateur pedigree, Hrgovic's only pro defeat came against Daniel Dubois in 2024.

He dismissed suggestions he was trying to play "mind games".

"I just tell you what I think. I think he's a kid, he's not mature enough. I think I'm the man. I'm a much better age, much more experienced. That's it," he said.

Itauma 'million times better' than Fury and Joshua - Hamed

Hrgovic taunts starting to wind me up - Itauma

Itauma v Hrgovic & Mayer v Cameron - all you need to know

Itauma kept a straight face as Hrgovic continued: "I will smash the kid on Saturday and I'll send him back to high school."

Itauma has stopped 12 of his 14 opponents and has built a reputation for his devastating speed, power and timing.

"The perfect performance will be to go a couple of rounds and close the job," he said. "Same script, different story."

But Hrgovic laughed off the suggestion.

"We'll see, man. No-one ever knocked me out any time in my life," he said. "I only got stopped by Dubois because of cuts and I was in terrible shape because of sickness."

The pair shared an intense face-off before Itauma left the stage.

Hrgovic then made light of Itauma's earlier claim that the Croat had been shaking during a previous face-off, by telling reporters: "Look how much I'm sweating. Look how scared I am."

Thursday's news conference was held at Studio 338 on London's Greenwich Peninsula, a venue more accustomed to booming club nights and electronic music than heavyweight boxing.

A relaxed, shirtless Hrgovic arrived half an hour before the event and waited patiently as a member of his team fanned him down.

Itauma arrived minutes before the start.

Hrgovic, now wearing a shirt with the buttons undone, described Saturday's fight as "the biggest fight of my life". He questioned whether Itauma was in the right shape and continued to try to provoke a reaction.

Itauma looked slightly agitated but, as he has throughout his career and the build-up to this fight, was reluctant to bite back.

"Me standing in front of a camera and microphone, saying what I'm going to do, doesn't mean much. I'm not trying to engage in any back and forth. My eyes are solely on Saturday," he said.

At 21 years and 244 days, Itauma would become the second-youngest heavyweight champion in boxing history, behind only Tyson, who won the WBC title at 20 years and 145 days in 1986.

Itauma would also become the second-youngest British world champion in any weight division, just 14 days older than 'Prince' Naseem Hamed, who was 21 years and 230 days old when he won the WBO featherweight title in 1995.

But Itauma said he was not interested in records.

"I'm not trying to become the second-youngest heavyweight champion of the world. I'm trying to beat Filip Hrgovic and become world heavyweight champion," he insisted.

The final word - keeping in tone with the event - went to Hrgovic, who ended the news conference by repeating his prediction: "I'll smash the kid, man."

title: Grealish keen on Everton, Man City look at Ndiaye
description: Jack Grealish's preference would be to make a return to Everton should he leave Manchester City in the remaining days of the transfer window, sources have told BBC Sport.
fullText:
Jack Grealish's preference would be to return to Everton should he leave Manchester City in the remaining days of the transfer window, sources have told BBC Sport.

And City hold an interest in signing Toffees winger Iliman Ndiaye, who has rejected multiple contract offers on Merseyside.

Grealish, 30, has appeared as a substitute in City's opening two games of the season, but new boss Enzo Maresca is open to letting the Englishman leave the club before Tuesday's transfer deadline.

Grealish spent last season with the Toffees, scoring twice and providing six assists in 20 appearances, before sustaining a season-ending foot injury in January.

Everton chief executive Angus Kinnear recently told BBC Radio Merseyside the club have "remained in contact" with the player.

Grealish's former club Aston Villa are also believed to still be interested in re-signing their ex-captain, but City sources say there have been no concrete offers from any club so far this summer.

Maresca said on Thursday: "Jack is here. Until the day he is, it my duty to try and help him to give us the best. In the next four, five days, we will see what happens. I speak with Jack almost every day."

Nidaye, meanwhile, is a player City are looking at.

Saudi side Al-Hilal held a strong interest in signing the Senegal international this summer, but the 26-year-old reportedly turned down the move.

David Moyes' side are under no pressure to sell Ndiaye, whose contract runs until 2029, and are likely to demand a significant fee in the region of £70m to even consider a sale.

Newly promoted Coventry City are in talks to sign City defender Stephen Mfuni on a season-long loan deal.

The 18-year-old made his first-team debut in the FA Cup third round last season before making eight appearances on loan at Watford in the Championship.

Are Moyes and Everton's owners on the same page?

Grealish back for Man City - but for how long?

Everton manager David Moyes would be very reluctant to lose Ndiaye, arguably his most creative player, but the Senegalese forward is known to want Champions League football and has rejected multiple offers to extend his current contract.

Moyes has made it clear he wants more quality in his squad, and while the sale of Ndiaye would be a huge blow, the potential return of Grealish may soften the blow.

Grealish was popular with Everton supporters but was sidelined from January with a stress fracture of the foot.

Everton chief executive Angus Kinnear confirmed in an interview with BBC Radio Merseyside that they had "remained in contact" with Grealish.

He said: "It's no secret he decided to have his rehabilitation here for the rest of the season when he didn't have to do that. He could have gone back to Manchester City.

"I think he is a player who has fallen in love with the right shade of blue but ultimately he is Manchester City player and we have to respect that."

Kinnear added: "We, the supporters and the team embraced him and treated him as if he was one of our own and gives us a very good platform to have a longer term conversation with him."

title: Fan backlash as gay World Cup star joins Saudi club
description: Spain forward Esther Gonzalez attracts backlash after signing for Saudi Women's Premier League side Al Qadsiah.
fullText:
Spain forward Esther Gonzalez has attracted backlash after signing for Saudi Women's Premier League side Al Qadsiah.

The 33-year-old agreed a mutual contract termination with National Women's Soccer League champions Gotham FC in July to temporarily step away from the sport to "attend to personal matters in Spain", according to the club's statement.

Gonzalez, whose contract was due to expire in 2027, said on Instagram the decision was "due to strictly personal reasons", adding New York-based Gotham will "always hold a special place in my heart".

However, on Sunday, Al Qadsiah announced the signing of the 2023 World Cup winner, sparking criticism from both Gotham fans over the nature of her departure, and from within the LGBTQ+ community.

Same-sex relationships and sexual activity are illegal in Saudi Arabia.

Fans on social media questioned her motivations and expressed concerns for her safety while Gotham supporters voiced their disappointment over the messaging around her exit and the club missing out on a transfer fee.

According to Spanish outlet El Mundo,, external Gonzalez has deleted all photos of herself with her wife and their first child, born in January, from her social media accounts since signing for Al Qadsiah.

Gonzalez is not the first footballer to encounter negative reactions for moving to Saudi Arabia, with England midfielder Jordan Henderson attracting criticism following his transfer to Saudi Pro League side Al-Ettifaq in 2023.

The move was described as a "slap in the face" by openly gay footballer Jake Daniels, who had received a message of support from Henderson when he came out.

The former Liverpool captain, who had previously shown his support for the LGBTQ+ community by wearing rainbow laces, a One Love armband, and writing messages of solidarity in a matchday programme, left Al-Ettifaq after six months.

Gonzalez won two NWSL titles, an NWSL Challenge Cup, and the Concacaf W Champions Cup in three seasons after moving to the United States from Real Madrid.

Al Qadsiah finished fourth in the Saudi Women's Premier League in 2025-26.

Gotham FC declined to comment when contacted by BBC Sport.

title: Villa sign Goretzka - what went wrong at Bayern and what will he bring?
description: Aston Villa complete the signing of former Bayern Munich midfielder Leon Goretzka on a free transfer.
fullText:
Aston Villa have completed the signing of former Bayern Munich midfielder Leon Goretzka on a free transfer.

The Germany international, 31, was available after leaving Bayern in the summer after eight years at the club.

"I had a bit of long vacation, and it was a process to find out what I really wanted. From the first moment, I had a really good feeling, and I'm really happy to be here," Goretzka said.

"I had a good feeling from the first conversation with the coach. Aston Villa is a really big club.

"I want to help the team to achieve their goals and to bring my experience that I have from my whole career.

"I'm really looking forward to playing in these kinds of big games every few days, and this is probably the biggest difference to the Bundesliga, where you have only several great games with big opponents."

Villa lost their opening Premier League fixture 4-0 at Brighton on Sunday and want boost their midfield options with Amadou Onana out until next year with a knee injury he suffered with Belgium at the World Cup.

Goretzka made 312 appearances for Bayern, scoring 51 times, during his time with the Bundesliga side. He also has 73 caps for Germany and made three appearances at the World Cup this summer.

He won seven league titles and the Champions League in 2020 with Bayern and will bring experience to Villa, who have lost several stars this summer.

Defender Ezri Konsa joined Arsenal for an initial £51m while forward Morgan Rogers was sold to Chelsea for £117m.

Midfield lynchpin Youri Tielemans joined Manchester United in July and left-back Lucas Digne returned to Paris St-Germain earlier this month.

Emery has also been unable to guarantee England striker Ollie Watkins will remain at Villa Park beyond the transfer deadline amid interest from Al-Hilal in Saudi.

For years, Goretzka was a cornerstone of Bayern Munich's midfield. But in recent years, the record German champions were not hiding their intentions to sell him for the right price.

He rejected a loan move to Galatasaray in 2024 while his sizeable wages at the Allianz Arena ruled out a number of potential destinations, as he was reluctant to accept a reduction in salary, and a move never came to fruition.

Instead his contract ran out in July, making him a free agent for the summer transfer window.

There was a time when Goretzka was considered Germany's best box-to-box midfielder.

His long build made him a force inside both penalty areas, while his ball-handling and tactical understanding helped him between the boxes. But his athleticism slowly faded over the years and younger players took his place.

Last season, Bayern manager Vincent Kompany primarily used Goretzka as a substitute, as did Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann during the World Cup this year.

Goretzka made three appearances for his national team, with 96 minutes in total playing time.

It is uncertain whether new Germany manager Jurgen Klopp will select Goretzka for international duty again.

A move to Aston Villa could certainly help the 31-year-old to revitalise his career, as he seemed stuck at Bayern where he spent a total of eight seasons.

When Goretzka arrived at Bayern from Schalke in 2018, he was revered as a modern type of midfielder, who could essentially play every position in the middle of the field.

Peter Neururer, Goretzka's coach at his hometown club of Bochum, called him a "once-in-a-century talent" when he was 18. The sky certainly seemed the limit in the 2010s.

While he has usually served as a number six, often playing alongside good friend Joshua Kimmich for Bayern and Germany, Goretzka has been used as an emergency centre-back and as a number 10 when needed.

Being slotted behind a striker highlighted Goretzka's strengths as a goalscorer.

His well-timed runs and stature made him a force in the air to convert crosses.

That skillset helped him at times to be picked by coaches when the competition in central midfield became increasingly tough.

As an example, Goretzka suddenly looked like a key player for Germany again in March and June 2025 when the national team played in the Nations League finals and he was employed in Nagelmann's starting line-up.

But these spells where he was able to shine became increasingly rare in recent years.

Injuries have plagued Goretzka from a young age to a degree that we will never exactly know where his true ceiling could have been in his 20s.

He rarely suffered severe injuries but had to deal with regular setbacks for a couple of years, and often in inopportune times.

Goretzka seemed to be at the height of his powers in the 2020-21 season, coming off a Champions League triumph with Bayern during the pandemic year.

But instead of being the engine for Germany's midfield at the European Championships in 2021, he missed the first group stage game due to the after-effect of a hamstring injury.

His only start came against England at Wembley in the round of 16.

When fit, Goretzka remained a starting XI player for Bayern until Kompany's arrival in 2024. And even then, following a first few months as a benchwarmer, he was able to fight his way back into the starting line-up.

However, the emergence of Aleksandar Pavlovic, a Munich-born midfielder and Bayern academy graduate, eventually sealed Goretzka's fate.

Villa close to £65m move for Chelsea's Jackson

Chelsea in contact over move for Villa goalkeeper Martinez

Goretzka repeatedly stated throughout the latter stage of his time at Bayern that he would fight for his spot but eventually had to accept the club hierarchy were not planning with him any longer.

The 31-year-old is certainly at a crossroads in his career. On the one hand, he has seven German championships, a Champions League title, a Club World Cup as well as 73 caps for Germany in his CV.

On the other hand, he and his camp thought he would attract the interest of major European clubs this summer, especially with him potentially signing on a free transfer. Goretzka was in concrete talks with AC Milan at one point, but that fell apart.

Aston Villa are likely not seen as a first-choice destination.

At the same time, it is not a given that Goretzka will be prominently featured in Unai Emery's line-up in the coming months.

Villa signed the rising Swiss midfielder Johan Manzambi, one of the best young players in the Bundesliga last season. Like Goretzka, the 20-year-old is a tall box-to-box player who possesses greater athletic prowess.

It is feasible that Manzambi could adapt himself to the speed of the Premier League faster than Goretzka who had trouble keeping up with the pace in the World Cup when he was brought on by Nagelsmann.

In essence, Villa are bringing in valuable experience but how much Goretzka has left to give on the field remains to be seen.

Watkins' departure would cut deepest - and Villa did not see it coming

Why 'woeful' Villa crumbled against Brighton

title: Arsenal only likely exit for Alvarez as striker skips training
description: Julian Alvarez has not attended Atletico Madrid training since being told privately that the club would not sell him to Barcelona.
fullText:
Julian Alvarez has not attended Atletico Madrid training since being told privately the club would not sell him to Barcelona and it appears the striker's only way out is with a move to Arsenal.

Sources told BBC Sport that Atletico communicated privately to Alvarez and his advisers earlier this week that they will not negotiate with the Catalan club over a move for the Argentina international.

The 26-year-old has since missed two consecutive days of training citing illness.

The La Liga club also released two public statements in the space of 24 hours reiterating their stance that Alvarez will not be granted his wish to join Barca in the coming days.

Atletico, however, are open to selling Alvarez to Arsenal and have held direct talks with the Premier League champions over what would be one of the biggest transfers of the summer.

Atleti director Mateu Alemany was in London last week, where he is understood to have met with Arsenal counterparts - and made clear his side would seek a fee of 150m euros (£128m).

Mikel Arteta is desperate to sign Alvarez this month but his steadfast desire to join Barcelona has seen Arsenal's pursuit halted.

However, it is understood discussions between Atletico and Arsenal over a club-to-club agreement for Alvarez have been positive.

Indeed, in the event of Alvarez giving Arsenal the green light to proceed with his signing in the coming days, a deal should move quickly.

On Wednesday, in response to comments from Barcelona president Joan Laporte in which he insisted they still wanted to sign Alvarez, Atletico released a statement that read: "There is 0% chance of selling him to Barca."

The Atletico board doubled down on their stance on Thursday, releasing their own statement that read: "The members of Atletico de Madrid's board of directors have unanimously expressed their absolute support for the club's decision to not negotiate the transfer of Julian Alvarez to FC Barcelona."

Alvarez's Arsenal dilemma amid summer's most bitter transfer tussle

title: Carragher facing bankruptcy petition over unpaid tax claim
description: Former Liverpool and England player turned pundit Jamie Carragher faces being declared bankrupt over an unpaid tax bill.
fullText:
Former Liverpool and England player turned pundit Jamie Carragher faces being declared bankrupt over an unpaid tax bill, said to be in the region of £700,000 and £800,000.

Documents seen by the BBC show that a case was filed against James Lee Duncan Carragher on Wednesday.

The 'bankruptcy petition' filed by lawyers representing HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) was first reported by City AM.

A spokesperson for HMRC told BBC Sport that it did not comment on individual cases, but a spokesperson added: "We take a supportive approach to dealing with customers who have tax debts and do everything we can to help those who engage with us to get out of debt, such as offering instalment plans.

"We only petition for bankruptcy as a last resort."

Carragher, who played for Liverpool between 1996 and 2013, regularly appears on Sky Sports' Premier League coverage, the Stick To Football show and CBS Sports' Champions League programming.

A spokesperson for Carragher told BBC Sport: "This is a private tax matter that should have been resolved sooner, and the appropriate steps are being taken today to settle it. It is understood that the matter will not proceed any further and will be resolved imminently."

Carragher is not the only footballer who has run into tax issues in his post-playing career.

Former England internationals David James, Wes Brown and Lee Hendrie have all been declared bankrupt, while former Liverpool team-mate Emile Heskey lost a legal battle over an unpaid £1.637m tax bill in 2024.

In 2025, Trevor Sinclair was made bankrupt after failing to pay a tax bill of more than £36,000. In the same year, Shaun Wright-Phillips was petitioned for bankruptcy by HMRC at London's High Court.

Last September, it was revealed that up to 200 footballers may have lost tens of millions of pounds, with some losing their homes and being made bankrupt.

Former England midfielder Danny Murphy - now a Match of the Day pundit - believes he lost roughly £5m because of "financial abuse".

title: Alcaraz draws Safiullin at US Open, tough start for Fery - who else plays who?
description: Carlos Alcaraz starts his US Open title defence against Russia's Roman Safiullin in the first serious examination of his fitness following a long-term wrist injury.
fullText:
Carlos Alcaraz will start his US Open title defence against Russia's Roman Safiullin in the first serious examination of his fitness following a long-term wrist injury.

Alcaraz, who won the men's title in New York last year, has not played a competitive singles match for more than four months because of inflammation in his playing right wrist.

The 23-year-old Spaniard missed this season's French Open and Wimbledon as a result of the issue, which did not require surgery, before making his return to court in the US Open mixed doubles alongside Serena Williams earlier this week.

Britain's surprise Wimbledon semi-finalist Arthur Fery returns to the Grand Slam stage with a first-round match against Italian 13th seed Lorenzo Musetti.

Novak Djokovic's latest quest for a standalone record 25th Grand Slam singles title starts against Argentina's Mariano Navone.

If he gets through that match, the 39-year-old Serb faces a challenging second-round match against either Italy's Matteo Berrettini - who Djokovic beat in the 2021 Wimbledon final - or three-time major champion Stan Wawrinka, in what will be the final major of the Swiss player's career after he was given a late wildcard.

Mensik & Muchova win US Open mixed doubles title

Wawrinka given late wildcard for US Open farewell

Despite his long absence, Alcaraz is still seeded second at Flushing Meadows behind Germany's Alexander Zverev, who faces Italy's Lorenzo Sonego in his opening match.

Zverev, looking for his second major title after finally breaking his duck at Roland Garros in June, is the top seed after Italy's Jannik Sinner withdrew with a knee injury.

In the women's draw, defending champion Aryna Sabalenka starts against Colombia's Camila Osorio.

Sabalenka goes into the US Open having topped the WTA rankings for 97 weeks, but knows her place remains under threat from reigning Australian Open champion Elena Rybakina, who has been drawn against American teenage wildcard Thea Frodin.

Two-time champion Venus Williams, 46, has been given a wildcard despite losing all 10 of her matches this season and faces 2020 Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin in the first round.

Fery, 24, produced a career-changing run at the All England Club in July, propelling him into the world's top 40 for the first time and securing his US Open debut in the process.

Fery narrowly missed out on a seeding and, having been drawn against 2025 quarter-finalist Musetti, has received a tough opener as a result.

A lot of attention will be placed on how the world number 37 fares in New York, where he leads a rather sparse British contingent in the absence of injured pair Jack Draper and Emma Raducanu.

Draper, who reached the 2024 semi-finals, withdrew last week because of a long-term arm injury, while 2021 champion Raducanu remains sidelined with the shin fracture which also forced her to miss Wimbledon.

British men's number one Cameron Norrie did manage to sneak into the seedings and the 29th seed plays France's Luca van Assche in his opening match.

Jan Choinski is currently the only other Briton in the men's draw after reaching the world's top 100 for the first time in June at the age of 30.

Choinski's reward for earning direct entry into a Grand Slam other than Wimbledon for the first time is a first-round contest with Dutch player Botic van de Zandschulp, who famously beat Alcaraz in the second round of the 2024 US Open.

Katie Boulter is the only Briton guaranteed a place in the women's draw through her ranking and meets American wildcard Carol Young Suh Lee, who is ranked 143rd in the world.

If Boulter wins a Grand Slam match for only the second time this year, the 30-year-old could meet Wimbledon finalist Karolina Muchova in the second round.

Six more Britons - Francesca Jones, Jacob Fearnley, Toby Samuel, Heather Watson, Harriet Dart and Harry Wendelken - aim to reach the main draws by winning their final qualifying matches on Thursday.
